summary: Add a nullable boolean column marketing_opt_in with DEFAULT false, backfill existing rows to FALSE, deploy the new version with a state‑only migration, retire the old version, and finally alter the column to NOT NULL, achieving zero‑downtime while keeping both versions consistent.
write_consistency: The column is created with DEFAULT false so the old version’s INSERT statements omit the column and receive FALSE. A backfill UPDATE sets any remaining NULLs to FALSE before deploy_new. After retire_old only the new version runs, and the final ALTER COLUMN SET NOT NULL guarantees no NULL values remain.

stages.description: Add nullable boolean column marketing_opt_in with default FALSE.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN marketing_opt_in BOOLEAN NULL DEFAULT false;

stages.description: Backfill all rows where marketing_opt_in is NULL with FALSE.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET marketing_opt_in = FALSE WHERE marketing_opt_in IS NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; it will no longer serve traffic.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ALTER COLUMN marketing_opt_in SET NOT NULL;
